valuation_philosophy: Enprise is a genuine NZX micro-cap (market cap ~NZ$8.2m at the current price) whose consolidated financial history is dominated by acquisition/dilution noise (Kilimanjaro Consulting consolidation FY2020, Recipe Marketing acquisition Aug-2024, repeated dilutive rights issues) rather than organic compounding. The valuation is built bottom-up from OWNER FCF, not reported FCF: reported FCF is first reduced by (a) IFRS-16 lease principal repayments (this is an office-based consulting business; lease liabilities of NZ$2.084m sit alongside NZ$1.085m of bank debt inside the CSV's NZ$3.169m 'TotalDebt' figure, and the cash-flow-statement lease repayment line is a real, recurring financing outflow that must be deducted to avoid overstating FCF), and (b) the 48%-owned Recipe Marketing non-controlling interest's share of consolidated earnings (Enprise shareholders are entitled to only 52% of that subsidiary's economics). SBC is verified NIL across all years (no share-based-payment expense line found in any Annual/Interim filing FY2018-H1FY2026; CSV StockBasedComp column is 0.0 throughout) so no SBC deduction is required. The 32.35%-owned Datagate Innovation and 6.4%-owned Vadacom Holdings stakes are equity-accounted / FVOCI investments that generate NO operating cash flow to the consolidated group (Datagate contributed an equity-accounted LOSS of NZ$0.03m in H1 FY2026) -- they are excluded entirely from the operating FCF build and instead added to equity value at their balance-sheet carrying value (NZ$0.864m + NZ$0.335m = NZ$1.199m combined at 31-Dec-2025) as a non-operating financial asset. On a mid-cycle basis (FY2020-FY2025, spanning both the post-dispute margin-cut years and the recovery), owner FCF has averaged just NZ$0.09m/yr and was NEGATIVE in 3 of the last 6 years (FY2022, FY2023, FY2025) -- this is a structurally thin-margin, capital/lease-intensive services business where EBITDA-to-FCF conversion is poor even in 'normal' years (Y5 base-case FCF/EBITDA conversion is only ~10%) because capex, lease principal, tax and NCI claims absorb most of EBITDA. Growth is modelled off ORGANIC revenue growth (~3.5-5%/yr, anchored to H1 FY2026's like-for-like Kilimanjaro +3.4% / iSell +4.9%), not the acquisition-augmented 15-16%/yr consolidated CAGR, because the latter is a step-change/M&A artefact (Kilimanjaro consolidation FY2019->FY2020 revenue +84%; Recipe Marketing added a full incremental segment from Aug-2024) that will not repeat organically. WACC is stacked to the high teens/low 20s reflecting four independently documented structural risks (illiquidity, single-vendor/MYOB dependency, thin capitalisation, key-person/CEO transition). Given the tiny FCF base, terminal value is Gordon-growth bound (not the EV/EBITDA cap) in the base and bull cases because FCF conversion, not the multiple cap, is the binding constraint -- this is the CONSERVATIVE outcome per the 'lower of Gordon/cap' rule, not an aggressive one. P/S (0.26-1.01x ex-outlier historical range, ~0.67x average) is used as the primary cross-check anchor rather than P/E or EV/EBITDA, because earnings and EBITDA are too close to zero/negative in most years for those multiples to be meaningful; the current price already implies a P/S of only ~0.33x, near the bottom of the historical range, showing the market itself is pricing this business cautiously. It is expected, and considered a correct output rather than a bug, that the base-case intrinsic value sits far below the current market price: the FCF-DCF and the P/S-anchor both point to a business the market is (rationally) not paying much for, and no upside has been manufactured to close that gap.

inputs.shares_outstanding_note: H1 FY2026 (31-Dec-2025) actual shares on issue per interim report note 5(a): 21,781,325, up from 20,068,057 at 30-Jun-2025 (FY2025 year-end) following a rights issue (NZ$0.76m, completed in the half) and the 14-Jan-2026 shortfall placement of 275,228 shares raising NZ$0.124m. This is the correct current count -- CSV's H1 FY2026 SharesOutstanding of 20.062m is a carry-forward/weighted-average artefact, not the period-end actual.
inputs.net_debt_methodology: Bank debt (borrowings, incl. overdraft per note 10) NZ$1.085m + lease liabilities NZ$2.084m (0.514 current + 1.570 non-current) = NZ$3.169m total debt (ties to CSV TotalDebt), LESS cash NZ$2.273m, all at 31-Dec-2025 (H1 FY2026). = +0.896m NET DEBT. Lease liabilities are deliberately INCLUDED (not the 'bank-debt-only' NZ$1.41m net-cash figure the company's own letter cites) because owner FCF already deducts the lease PRINCIPAL repayment as a financing-like cash outflow -- excluding the matching lease liability from net debt would double-count the benefit of that deduction. The company's cited 'net cash NZ$1.41m' nets bank borrowings/overdraft against cash only and excludes lease liabilities entirely; both figures are reconciled here for transparency.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Owner FCF is NOT a single-year figure for this business -- reported FCF is tiny and erratic (FY2020 2.566, FY2021 1.859, FY2022 -0.632, FY2023 -1.330, FY2024 1.182, FY2025 0.201) and even more so after the lease-principal deduction (FY2020 2.151, FY2021 1.097, FY2022 -1.244, FY2023 -1.925, FY2024 0.650, FY2025 -0.208). last_fcf here is the 6-year (FY2020-FY2025) MID-CYCLE AVERAGE owner FCF used as the qualitative anchor for the projection base; the actual DCF projection is built bottom-up from FY2025 revenue (NZ$24.973m) and component EBITDA margins/capex/lease/tax/NCI ratios (see projections.base), not by growing this single figure forward.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 reported FCF (OperatingCashFlow 1.025 - CapEx 0.824). H1 FY2026 reported FCF was +0.307 (owner FCF +0.029 after deducting the H1 lease repayment of 0.278).
inputs.sbc_source: verified NIL -- no 'share-based payment', 'share option' or equity-settled compensation expense line found in any Annual Report (FY2018-FY2025) or Interim Report (H1 FY2019-H1 FY2026) cash-flow reconciliation, income statement or notes; CSV StockBasedComp column is 0.0 in every populated year. The only equity-related financing items are cash rights issues, shortfall placements, and minority NCI share subscriptions/purchases in Kilimanjaro/iSell/Recipe Marketing -- none are SBC.
inputs.lease_note: IFRS-16 lease liabilities (office leases for Kilimanjaro/Recipe Marketing/iSell premises in NZ and Australia) totalled NZ$2.084m at 31-Dec-2025 (0.514 current + 1.570 non-current), embedded within the CSV's TotalDebt figure alongside NZ$1.085m of bank debt. The financing-activities 'Repayment of lease liabilities' cash-flow line is deducted from reported FCF in every historical year and modelled forward as ~2.0-2.2% of revenue (base/bear) or 1.8% (bull) in the projections, consistent with the historical range of 2.0-4.7% of revenue.
inputs.nci_note: Recipe Marketing Limited (HubSpot/CRM marketing partner) is 52%-owned by Kilimanjaro Consulting Limited (itself 100%-owned by Enprise), establishing a 48% non-controlling interest from the 26-Aug-2024 acquisition. NCI balance was NEGATIVE NZ$0.333m at 31-Dec-2025 (NZ$0.222m negative at 30-Jun-2025), reflecting accumulated losses attributable to the minority since acquisition (consolidated P&L 'Non-Controlling Interest' line: FY2025 -0.028, FY2024 -0.039 [pre-Recipe, relates to the earlier iSell Pty NCI], FY2023 -0.473 [iSell NCI]). Projections deduct an estimated 4-6% of consolidated NOPAT as the minority claim, reflecting Recipe Marketing's modest and currently loss-making contribution to the group.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not material/separately disclosed as a distinct line; the company runs net finance COST (net finance cost NZ$0.273m in FY2025, i.e. interest expense on bank debt/leases exceeds any interest earned on the small cash balance), so no interest-income strip is required or would be material to the DCF.
inputs.uncovered_dilution_note: Not modelled via the buyback-vs-SBC formula (SBC is nil) -- instead, forward dilution is modelled directly as a base/bull/bear annual share-growth assumption (1.5-5.0%/yr) reflecting Enprise's demonstrated repeated recourse to dilutive capital raises (shares on issue: 9.578m FY2018 -> 15.901m FY2020 -> 17.430m FY2023 -> 20.068m FY2024 -> 21.781m H1 FY2026, i.e. more than doubled in under 8 years) to shore up its thin balance sheet.

equity_accounted_investments.treatment: Added to equity value at balance-sheet carrying value (31-Dec-2025) as a non-operating financial asset. Neither generates operating cash flow captured in the consolidated FCF build (equity-accounted results and FVOCI fair-value movements sit below the operating-profit line and are excluded from the projected FCF entirely). No independent mark-to-market or DCF-of-the-stake was available/warranted for holdings this small relative to the group (carrying value = ~15% of Enprise's own market cap); carrying value is the conservative, auditable figure.

historical_growth.eps_note: Not computed -- EPS/NI has been negative or near-zero in 4 of the last 8 years (FY2019, FY2022, FY2023 large loss, FY2024/25 near-breakeven), making CAGR mathematically undefined/meaningless.
historical_growth.fcf_note: Owner FCF CAGR not computed -- the series is negative in 3 of 6 years (FY2022 -1.244, FY2023 -1.925, FY2025 -0.208) making CAGR undefined. Mid-cycle (FY2020-25) owner FCF average is NZ$0.087m/yr; recent 3-year (FY2023-25) average is NEGATIVE NZ$0.494m/yr, indicating deterioration, not growth, in owner FCF terms even as reported revenue grew.
historical_growth.growth_rate_rationale: Neither the revenue CAGR (10-16%, acquisition-augmented) nor the equity CAGR (-22% to -32%, distorted by the FY2023 NZ$7.7m goodwill impairment and subsequent dilutive-raise rebuild) is usable as a forward growth driver. The selected 4.0% base-case starting growth rate is anchored to H1 FY2026's like-for-like organic growth: Kilimanjaro (the core business, ~93% of group revenue) grew 3.4% H1-on-H1, and iSell grew 4.9% H1-on-H1, both with Recipe Marketing already owned for the full comparative period (acquired Aug-2024). This organic rate is materially BELOW the historical consolidated CAGR because the latter embeds the FY2020 Kilimanjaro consolidation step-change and the FY2025 Recipe Marketing acquisition, neither of which recurs mechanically.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue 5yr CAGR (15.0%) vs organic-growth proxy (~4.0%) diverges by ~11 percentage points -- flagged and NOT resolved by picking the higher figure. Equity CAGR is deeply negative (-22% to -32%) purely due to the FY2023 impairment/dilution cycle and is explicitly NOT used as the growth driver (would imply an economically nonsensical shrinking business alongside growing revenue).

wacc_rationale.illiquidity_premium_note: NZX micro-cap: market cap ~NZ$8.2m at the current price, no identified sell-side analyst coverage, thin daily trading volume typical of sub-NZ$10m NZX names.
wacc_rationale.vendor_dependency_premium_note: Kilimanjaro (the core, ~93% of group revenue) is contractually and economically dependent on a single software vendor, MYOB. MYOB attempted a unilateral ~43% margin cut in 2022 (worth ~NZ$935k/yr), requiring an Australian Federal Court injunction and 2023 litigation settlement to resolve. The settlement guaranteed Exo partner rights only 'until at least 31 December 2025' -- that date has now passed (valuation date 2026-08-10) with management's H1 FY2026 letter referencing an 'extended runway for Exo that MYOB has committed to' but no independently verified public confirmation of formal renewal terms was located in the filings reviewed.
wacc_rationale.thin_capitalisation_premium_note: Total equity NZ$3.117m (31-Dec-2025) against NZ$12.727m of total liabilities; the FY2023 NZ$7.7m goodwill/intangible impairment erased ~90% of equity in a single year and required repeated dilutive rights issues (FY2024, FY2026) to rebuild the balance sheet. Net tangible assets per share have been negative in recent periods.
wacc_rationale.key_person_premium_note: Managing Director/CEO Ronald Baskind (Kilimanjaro founder, ~20 years' involvement, described by the Board as instrumental to the group's success) departs 4-September-2026; interim CEO appointed while a permanent search proceeds. Elevated execution risk during the Exo-to-Acumatica transition and ongoing MYOB relationship management.
wacc_rationale.wacc_bull_note: Lower stacked premiums once CEO transition is managed smoothly and Exo/MYOB relationship terms are confirmed favourably.
wacc_rationale.wacc_bear_note: Higher stacked premiums if MYOB relationship deteriorates further or CEO transition proves disruptive, compounding the existing thin-capitalisation fragility.

base.growth_rates_note: Organic growth tapering from ~5% (current run-rate) toward 3% terminal, reflecting continued ~7%/yr MYOB Exo on-premise attrition being progressively offset by Acumatica cloud migration and Recipe Marketing cross-sell, but with no further step-change acquisitions assumed.
base.ebitda_margin_path_note: Ramps from the currently depressed H1 FY2026 run-rate (annualized EBITDA margin is slightly negative) back toward, but conservatively below, the ex-dispute-year historical average of 10.4% (FY2020, FY2021, FY2024, FY2025 average; FY2022-23 MYOB-dispute years excluded as outliers). Never approaches the FY2020 peak of 18.4%, reflecting structural margin pressure from wage inflation and the Exo-to-Acumatica transition.

bull.narrative: Successful Exo-to-Acumatica transition and Recipe Marketing cross-sell drive above-organic growth; utilisation and margins recover toward (but below) the FY2020 peak; MYOB Exo rights formally renewed on favourable terms; smooth CEO transition; DTA (NZ$1.9m recognised) shelters cash tax modestly; fewer dilutive raises as profitability improves.

bear.narrative: MYOB Exo partner rights not renewed on acceptable terms (or margin further compressed), continuing the H1 FY2026 operating-loss trend; CEO transition disrupts client/staff relationships; Exo attrition outpaces Acumatica/Recipe Marketing growth, revenue declines from Y4; more frequent dilutive capital raises required to sustain the thin balance sheet.

base.terminal_bound_note: Gordon (FCF-based) binds because owner-FCF conversion is structurally poor (~10% of EBITDA in Y5) -- this is the CONSERVATIVE outcome of the min(Gordon, cap) rule, not an aggressive one; using the 6.7x EV/EBITDA cap instead would value the business far higher (implied cap TV of NZ$14.25m vs Gordon's NZ$1.30m) than its cash-generation history supports.
base.terminal_pct_of_value_note: Not meaningful -- enterprise value is negative (interim-period cash burn exceeds the small discounted terminal value), so a percentage-of-EV split is not informative here.

bear.terminal_bound_note: Gordon is undefined/negative (terminal FCF is negative), so the EV/EBITDA cap is used as the floor-type terminal value on the barely-positive Y5 EBITDA (NZ$0.371m).
bear.equity_value_floor_note: Uncapped equity value is negative (-2.481), which is not a meaningful economic outcome for ordinary equity (shareholders are not liable for further losses beyond invested capital once operations cease adding value) -- equity value is floored at the net-cash-plus-investments 'shell' value (i.e. treating the operating business as worth zero, not negative): -net_debt + equity_investments = -0.896 + 1.199 = 0.303.

entry_price.methodology: Base-case interim FCFs (Y1-Y5) discounted at the 15% hurdle, plus the base-case Gordon terminal value (computed at WACC 19%, the fair price a buyer pays at exit) discounted back at the 15% hurdle, plus the equity-accounted investments carrying value, less net debt, divided by year-5 projected share count.

base.note: Entry price sits close to (and marginally below) the base-case intrinsic value (NZ$0.0068), consistent with the sanity property that a 15% hurdle close to the 19% base WACC produces an entry price near intrinsic value; here the hurdle (15%) is actually BELOW the base WACC (19%), so the entry price is slightly ABOVE base IV, as expected. Both figures are far below the current NZ$0.375 price -- reflecting the genuinely thin owner-FCF economics of this business, not a modelling error.
base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

entry_price.method: PV at the 15% hurdle of the interim owner FCFs plus a terminal value REBUILT AT THE HURDLE RATE (min(Gordon@15%, cap x FCF_N)), less net debt, divided by the TERMINAL-year share count the model dilutes to. Computed for all three scenarios and probability-weighted 2026-09-01: previously only the base case carried an entry price, which silently assumes the base case is certain.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows = WACC 17-21%, Columns = terminal growth 1.0-3.0%, base-case scenario. Intrinsic value is uniformly low (NZ$0.002-0.014) across the entire sensitivity range because the base case's terminal-year FCF is tiny (NZ$0.216m against a 25.25m projected share count) -- the model is far more sensitive to the underlying margin/capex/lease/NCI assumptions than to WACC or terminal growth within plausible ranges.

implied_multiples_at_base_iv.note: P/E and EV/EBITDA are not meaningful sanity anchors given near-zero/negative FY2025 NI (NZ$0.126m) and thin EBITDA (NZ$1.065m) -- see P/S below as the primary anchor.
implied_multiples_at_base_iv.ev_ebitda_fy2025_actual_at_base_iv: base IV implies EV of ~-0.13m vs FY2025 EBITDA 1.065m -- not meaningful (negative EV)

outliers_excluded: FY2021 (post-COVID speculative micro-cap spike, price 2.366, P/S 2.37x)
FY2022 (MYOB dispute year, P/S 0.99x borderline but revenue base already stressed)
ps_anchor.current_price_implied_ps_note: Current mcap NZ$8.168m (21.781m shares x NZ$0.375) / FY2025 revenue NZ$24.973m = 0.327x -- near the BOTTOM of the ex-outlier historical range (0.26-1.01x), confirming the market is already pricing Enprise cautiously, consistent with this DCF's low intrinsic value.
ps_anchor.base_iv_implied_ps_note: Base-case IV (NZ$0.0068/share) implies a P/S of only ~0.006x -- BELOW even the lowest historical P/S (0.26x, FY2019). This signals the pure FCF-Gordon DCF is more punitive than the market's own historical floor multiple for this stock, because the terminal-year FCF conversion (10% of EBITDA) assumed in the base case is worse than what the stock has historically traded on an EBITDA/sales basis. The P/S-implied fair value range (NZ$0.30-1.16/share using the historical 0.26-1.01x range against FY2025 revenue) is therefore presented as a wider, complementary anchor -- the probability-weighted DCF output of NZ$0.077 sits within, but toward the low end of, a defensible range once this cross-check is considered.
ps_anchor.diagnosis: The FCF-DCF (which drives the formal valuation/entry-price outputs per the prescribed methodology) is more conservative than a pure P/S-multiple approach would suggest, because it fully captures the lease/capex/NCI/tax drag on cash conversion that a revenue multiple does not see. Both anchors agree directionally: this is a thin-margin, structurally low-multiple micro-cap where the current NZ$0.375 price already reflects meaningful caution, and a base-case DCF value materially below the current price is a defensible, non-manufactured output rather than a modelling artefact.

pb_anchor.note: Current P/B (2.4-2.6x) is HIGH relative to the historical ex-outlier average (~1.25x per the task brief), driven by the denominator (owners' equity NZ$3.450m) being unusually small post the FY2023 impairment -- not by an elevated market valuation in dollar terms. This multiple is DE-EMPHASISED as a sanity anchor given how thin/distorted the equity base is.

sanity_check.diagnosis_summary: No mechanical trip triggered (upside is deeply negative, not >100% positive, so no upside-overstatement flag applies). The base-case IV is extremely low in absolute terms; this has been cross-checked against the P/S historical range (which independently implies a wider but still sub-NZ$0.375 fair-value band in most of its range) and is judged a genuine reflection of thin, erratic owner FCF rather than a modelling error. The probability-weighted IV (NZ$0.077, -79.5% vs current price) is presented as the headline output, with the P/S-anchor range (NZ$0.30-1.16) disclosed alongside as a wider band for context.

key_judgment_calls: Used H1 FY2026 (31-Dec-2025) actual shares on issue (21.781m) rather than the CSV's carried-forward/weighted-average H1 FY2026 figure (20.062m), because the interim report note 5(a) explicitly reconciles opening 20,068,057 to closing 21,781,325 shares within the half via the rights issue.

Included IFRS-16 lease liabilities (NZ$2.084m) in net debt alongside bank debt (NZ$1.085m), for consistency with deducting lease principal repayments from owner FCF -- using the company's own 'net cash NZ$1.41m' framing (which excludes leases) would be internally inconsistent with the FCF treatment.

Verified SBC as NIL directly from filing text search (no share-based-payment expense line in any year FY2018-H1FY2026) rather than assuming an undisclosed figure -- no adjustment needed, no warning banner required.

Valued the 32.35% Datagate and 6.4% Vadacom stakes at balance-sheet carrying value (NZ$1.199m combined) added to equity value as a non-operating asset, rather than attempting a separate DCF/mark on holdings this small relative to group size, since no reliable independent valuation data was available in the filings.

Deducted an estimated 4-6% of consolidated NOPAT as the Recipe Marketing 48% NCI claim across scenarios, based on Recipe Marketing's modest revenue contribution and currently loss-making status (NCI balance is negative, i.e. minority shareholders have absorbed losses to date).

Selected organic revenue growth (~3.5-5%/yr, from H1 FY2026 like-for-like segment growth) as the base-case driver rather than the acquisition-augmented consolidated revenue CAGR (10-16%) or the deeply negative equity CAGR (-22% to -32%, an FY2023-impairment artefact) -- both alternatives were explicitly rejected as unrepresentative of forward organic economics.

Stacked four independent WACC premiums (illiquidity +2.5%, MYOB vendor dependency +2.25%, thin capitalisation +1.75%, key-person/CEO transition +1.0%) on a 10.5% unadjusted cost of equity, landing at 19.0% base WACC -- within the 18-20% range the task brief anticipated.

Floored the bear-case equity value at the net-cash-plus-investments 'shell' value (NZ$0.303m, IV NZ$0.0109/share) rather than allowing the uncapped Gordon/cap terminal-value math to produce a negative equity value (-NZ$2.481m), consistent with the ALF.NZ precedent that ordinary shareholders are not liable for further losses beyond invested capital.

Did NOT manufacture upside to close the gap between the FCF-DCF's very low base-case IV (NZ$0.0068) and the current NZ$0.375 market price -- the wide P/S-anchor cross-check (NZ$0.30-1.16 historical range) is disclosed transparently as a complementary, less-conservative read rather than substituted as the headline number, per the explicit task instruction.
